incidents.title: Apollo 1: a flash fire in pure oxygen

what.quote: The astronauts would be wearing spacesuits with the spacecraft’s hatches closed and the cabin pressurized with 100% oxygen
what.source: NASA Safety and Mission Assurance: Apollo 1 case study

what.quote: Because of the pure oxygen atmosphere, the fire spread quickly, causing a rapid rise in temperature and pressure that led to the rupture of the Command Module pressure vessel
what.source: NASA Safety and Mission Assurance: Apollo 1 case study

what.quote: Air Force pathologists concluded the astronauts perished from asphyxia from carbon monoxide and other toxic gases resulting from the fire
what.source: NASA Safety and Mission Assurance: Apollo 1 case study

what.quote: NASA’s long history of successes in testing and launching space vehicles with pure oxygen environments at 16.7 p.s.i. and lower pressures led to overconfidence and complacency
what.says: The congressional summary of the review

ties.text: Pure oxygen at 16.7 psi is on the atmosphere map as a historical point. No PSI test row lies anywhere near it, and none lies near today's suit atmosphere either.
Gases, not flames, killed the crew. Saffire reached the same ordering sixty years later: carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide rose more than temperature and pressure.

incidents.title: Apollo 13: insulation burned inside an oxygen tank

what.quote: During the final test on the launch pad, the heaters were left on for an extended period and reached temperatures around 1000 degrees Fahrenheit, degrading the Teflon insulation
what.says: The cause, years before the flight
what.source: NASA Safety and Mission Assurance: Apollo 13 case study

what.quote: the explosion in tank number two also damaged tank number one, making use of the fuel cells impossible and threatening the eventual loss of all electrical power and water
what.source: NASA Safety and Mission Assurance: Apollo 13 case study

what.quote: Thankfully, a lesson learned from the Apollo I fire prevented arcing from happening, as a major redesign added increased insulation to better protect the wiring
what.source: NASA Safety and Mission Assurance: Apollo 13 case study

ties.text: A material judged acceptable was not, once the conditions around it changed. That is the question the ranking and the atmosphere map ask of every test: under which conditions was this measured?

incidents.title: Mir: a fire that fed itself

what.quote: the canister ignited, shooting a three-foot flame with sparks and bits of molten metal across the module and generating a large quantity of dense smoke
what.source: NASA History: 25 Years Ago, Fire Aboard Space Station Mir

what.quote: The flame blocked the evacuation route to the Soyuz spacecraft docked at the aft end of Kvant-1
what.source: NASA History: 25 Years Ago, Fire Aboard Space Station Mir
NASA History: 25 Years Ago, Fire Aboard Space Station Mir

ties.text: This is one of the cases set against "a fire will self-extinguish if ventilation is shut off".
The page calls the device a solid-fuel oxygen generator. That it fed its own flame is our reading.

what.quote: New backpack system weighs only 20 pounds for 30 minute air supply, 13 pounds less than conventional firefighting tanks

ties.text: Breathing protection is the first step of every fire response on the station too. What the crew breathes while the fans are off is the subject of the alarm pages.

earth.title: A detector that tells smoke from dust

what.quote: can discriminate between combustion particles and extraneous matters such as dust
what.says: First used in space shuttle orbiters

what.quote: it senses and signals the presence of a fire condition before appearance of flame and smoke

ties.quote: Fundamental research in microgravity highlighted the vastly different particulate size associated with flames in microgravity
ties.says: Why the problem is harder in orbit
ties.source: A Researcher's Guide to: Combustion Science (NASA)

ties.text: Smoke-particle measurements in PSI: SAME, SAME-R and the dust test DAFT.

what.quote: lightweight, fire-resistant, heat-protective materials originally developed for use in astronauts' space suits or in spacecraft components which require thermal protection
what.source: NASA Spinoff: New Technology for the Fire Attire (1982)

ties.text: Material choice is the oldest fire control in spaceflight, and the one the Apollo 1 review turned on. The ranking page orders the PSI records by how directly they test materials.
